evidence.quote: The patient was promptly treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate, resulting in resolution of tetany within hours. In the following days, repeat electrolyte testing showed marked improvement in both magnesium and potassium levels

clinical_significance.statement: Authors document MgSO4 following carpal tetany and subsequent improvement of magnesium/potassium. Exact plotted estimates remain visual-only, not new text-derived laboratory facts.

limitations: No new diagnosis is inferred from plotted eGFR or potassium levels. Printed bars differ in detail from unspecific text and are retained as separate visual evidence.

visual.general_description: A colored diagnostic flowchart branches from persistent hypokalemia into pseudohypokalemia and urinary/acid-base/blood-pressure pathways.
visual.detailed_description: Top blue box Persistent hypokalemia forks False(left) to blue Pseudohypokalemia and No further workup; True(right) to green Proceed with U K/U cr. A threshold U K/U cr >13mEq/g splits No(left) to extrarenal-loss/transcellular-shift causes and Yes(right) to orange acid-base branches. The middle orange box reads Metabolic alkalosis or normal serum HCO3−; a right orange box literally reads Metabolic alkalosis - RTA. Middle branch splits into High blood pressure(renal artery stenosis, hyperaldosteronism, Cushing’s syndrome) and Normal/Low blood pressure. The latter splits into urinary chloride<20mmol/L(diuretics, vomiting) and >20mmol/L(diuretics, magnesium depletion, Bartter, Gitelman). Boxes are connected by solid black lines/arrows; no panel letters or case-specific marker highlights appear.
